subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete numbers we discussed so your team can validate and we can size Dedicated accordingly.

Call recap (short):
- FinTechCo is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated for production due to data locality and SLA needs, but you want a fallback to Hosted for burst traffic and are evaluating Private VPC for regulated flows.
- Primary workload: real-time customer support & KYC enrichment (low latency, high QPS bursts).

Sizing inputs you confirmed:
- Steady TPS (reqs/sec): ~150 req/s average
- Peak TPS (burst): up to ~300 req/s for short periods (1-10 min)
- Average token mix per request: ~400 tokens total (prompt ~280 / completion ~120)
- 95th pct latency target: <250ms for text-gen flows
- Expected concurrency during peak: ~200 concurrent requests
- Model preference: high-performance open model (you mentioned H100 as preferred hardware)

Attachments: I attached a short sizing worksheet (dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx) and your network diagram you shared (network-diagram.png) — I filled in the call inputs so we have a starting point.

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) You confirm the numbers above (TPS, tokens, concurrency).
2) We produce 2 sizing options: (A) performance-first: H100-based cluster + recommended autoscale thresholds; (B) cost-optimized: A100 + quantization recommendations.
3) 30-minute follow-up to walk through the sizing options and timeline for provisioning.

If the inputs in the attached sheet look good, I’ll run our internal sizing calc and share node counts / estimated cost ranges by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Aditya Rao

aditya.rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0179

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Aditya — helpful recap. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Steady state: 140-160 req/s (so 150 is fine to use).
- Peak bursts: yes, up to ~300 req/s but typically <5 minutes; some events could push 400 req/s for <1 minute during promotions.
- Token mix: prompt-heavy, agreed on ~400 tokens average. We do have a minority of longer prompts (1-2% >1k tokens) for batch enrichment.
- Concurrency: 200 is a safe working number; we care most about p95 latency and graceful degradation rather than 100% zero-droppage.

Two additional asks:
1) What is the expected provisioning lead time for Dedicated (start to provision test cluster) and for Private VPC? Procurement needs an estimate.
2) Can you outline the fallback behavior to Hosted API during overload? We need to understand how routing and data flows would work for the sensitive vs non-sensitive traffic.

We’d like to schedule the follow-up sizing review on Thu or Fri — I’m available 10-12 PT both days.

Thanks —
Sarah
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
FinTechCo
sarah.liu@fintechco.com

Thanks Sarah — confirmed on the numbers and the longer tail for 1-2% high-token requests. Answers to your two asks below and proposed next steps.

Provisioning lead times:
- Dedicated test cluster (proof-of-concept): typically 2-5 business days once we have network & firewall rules and an SOW in place.
- Private VPC: 7-14 business days (depends on KMS/HSM, peering setup, and customer change window).

Fallback behavior to Hosted API:
- Policy-based routing: we can route by request attributes (customer_id, route, or header). You can route sensitive traffic to Dedicated/Private and non-sensitive to Hosted.
- Overflow/burst handling: when Dedicated is at capacity we can failover specific routes to Hosted (configurable), with options: (A) redirect to Hosted for best-effort low-latency; (B) queue requests with graceful backpressure; (C) return rate-limit responses. We’ll document recommended policies for your SLA targets.

Sizing options I’ll deliver (tomorrow EOD):
- Perf-first option: 6x H100 nodes (steady 150 req/s, peak buffer to 300-400 req/s with autoscale/burst capacity); includes KV cache tuning and batching config for 400-token average.
- Cost-optimized option: 10x A100 nodes with INT8 quantization recommendations (lower throughput per node but cheaper infra).

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Fri 10:30 PT to review the sizing sheet and agree on an option? I’ll include Marissa (solutions) so we can cover network and procurement checklists.

Links: HubSpot deal DL-2026-0179 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/FinTechCo) and I’ve uploaded the sizing workbook here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-dedicated-sizing

I’ll also attach an internal cost calc for Marissa’s reference after this thread.

—
Aditya

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: FinTechCo recommended sizing & pricing notes (DL-2026-0179)

Marissa — internal note following Sarah’s confirmations. Putting recommended config and asks for solutions/procurement: 

Recap of confirmed inputs: steady 150 req/s, peak 300-400 req/s (short bursts), avg 400 tokens, concurrency ~200, 1-2% >1k tokens. Customer prefers H100 for perf.

Our recommended baseline (to present on Fri):
- Perf-first: 6x H100 nodes (NVIDIA H100), KV cache enabled, batching tuned for 400-token average, autoscale thresholds to add 2 nodes at 220 req/s and up to 2 additional nodes for spikes to 400 req/s.
- Cost-opt: 10x A100 nodes with INT8 quantization / batching changes (adds risk on quality for ~10% of prompts, call that out).
- Concurrency: We will configure 200 concurrent request slots with queueing/backpressure and a hosted fallback policy.
- Network: need firewall rules, peering info; procurement wants provisioning lead time 2-5 days for test cluster.

Action items for Marissa:
1) Review the internal-costs-calc.csv and confirm margin target for Dedicated sizing (I used 30% gross margin target).
2) Prepare a short SOW draft (bullet list) and procurement checklist for customer (I’ll share after call).
3) Join Fri 10:30 PT call with Sarah — I’ll send invite.

If that looks good I’ll present the perf-first vs cost-optimized options on the call and capture which variant we should price into the SOW.

—
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
